mcat_description.short: A polyhouse is a prefabricated protected cultivation structure with a GI tubular frame covered by UV-stabilised polyethylene film, sold as a complete turnkey structure, kit, or material set for year-round crop farming in India.
mcat_description.long: A polyhouse (also called a poly greenhouse) is a framed agricultural structure covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film that creates a controlled microclimate for growing vegetables, flowers, and high-value crops under protected conditions. In India, the dominant commercial form is the Naturally Ventilated Poly House (NVPH), built with hot-dip galvanised (HDG) GI pipes conforming to NHB/MIDH technical standards, with gutter heights of 4.0–4.5 m and ridge heights of 6.0–6.5 m. Structures are eligible for 50–65% government subsidy under NHM/NHB/MIDH schemes, making subsidy compliance a critical purchase criterion. Sellers offer complete turnkey construction, DIY kits, or individual structural materials (GI pipes, UV film, insect nets, clamps), with customisation by area, crop type, and agro-climatic zone.

market_context: In India, 'polyhouse' and 'poly house' are used interchangeably and refer specifically to a greenhouse structure covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film, distinguishing it from glass greenhouses or shade net houses. The Naturally Ventilated Poly House (NVPH) is the dominant commercial form, accounting for the majority of installations, due to its cost-effectiveness and eligibility for 50–65% government subsidy under NHM/NHB/MIDH schemes. NHB and MIDH have published detailed technical standards specifying GI pipe grades (IS 1161, hot-dip galvanised per IS 4759:2019, 275 GSM zinc coating), structural dimensions (gutter height 4.0–4.5 m, ridge height 6.0–6.5 m), and UV film specifications (200 micron, 3–5 layer co-extruded, ISI certified), which define the minimum acceptable quality for subsidy-eligible structures. Fan & Pad (environmentally controlled) polyhouses are a premium sub-segment suited to hot/arid climates, used for high-value crops and hydroponics. Key Indian manufacturers and empanelled vendors include Agriplast Protected Cultivation (Tamil Nadu), Jain Irrigation Systems (Maharashtra), Netafim India, Govind Greenhouse (Pune), AgroDome Projects (Gujarat), and Inhydro. The Israeli greenhouse design influence is notable — several Indian manufacturers cite Israeli technology for aerodynamic frame design and ventilation engineering. Buyers in this category are highly price-sensitive and subsidy-driven; the NHB/MIDH benchmark rate is a key reference point for procurement decisions. Polyhouse film brands such as Ginegar (Israel) are specifically searched by buyers, indicating brand awareness at the film/material level even when the structure itself is commodity-priced.
